name: Base Sepolia USDC -> Sentrix Testnet sUSDC

destination.hypErc20ImplVariant: HypERC20Capped (v2026-05-21, cap-aware fork of stock HypERC20)

security.sentrixSafeBaseLimitation: Address has no code on Base Sepolia. The collateral router's onlyOwner functions cannot be invoked from this chain — Base side is effectively immutable. A real Gnosis Safe deployment on Base + router migration is the only path to recover admin control there. Tracked as separate work.

sentrixIsm.swappedReason: Audit C-1: old 1-of-1 ISM had validator == deployer EOA. Replaced via SentrixSafe.execTransaction with a 2-of-3 set of independent validator EOAs.

baseSepoliaIsm.knownRisk: Validator == deployer EOA and the collateral router is owner-less (see sentrixSafeBaseLimitation). Compromise of deployer key alone is sufficient to forge an inbound message and drain locked USDC. Cannot be fixed without redeploying the collateral router under a real Base-side Safe.

caps.denom: 6-decimal sUSDC base units (perTxCap=100 sUSDC, dailyCap=1000 sUSDC, totalMintCap=10000 sUSDC)
caps.enforcement: On-chain via HypERC20Capped._transferTo. Outbound burns are uncapped (user can always exit what they hold). Caps only block inbound mint path so the worst-case impact of a forged ISM message is bounded.

openAuditFindings: H-2: Hook / IGP not set on either router. Only meaningful once an auto-relayer is running — manual relay flow does not need IGP.

H-3 + H-4: No Hyperlane validator / relayer agents running. Every bridge tx requires manual `cast wallet sign` + `cast send process`. Production needs both agents on dedicated hosts with isolated keys.
M-1: Operationally the deployer key still doubles as the relayer key. Even with C-1 fixed, this concentrates the spend-side. Separate to a dedicated relayer EOA when H-4 lands.
Base-side limitation: collateral router is owner-less; admin functions unreachable. Migration ticket required to introduce a real Base-side Safe.
